label: refined

reasoning.text: In the ISO render the 16x12 board is an oversized flat slab (bounds.radius ~10, over the ~9 limit) so the floorplan reads as a dark featureless plate with low parts crouching on it; the TOP view is the only legible angle. The four butterfly clusters used a single opaque 'housing' box per cluster — a build-test failure because the paper's whole point is the symmetric add/sub operators and the DSP multiplier, which were collapsed into one ALU box rather than modeled as distinct members. The conflict-free schedule controller (the central algorithmic contribution) was missing entirely, and primitives were almost all boxes.
gaps: Add an exploded copy of one butterfly cluster floating ~2.5 m above the board to make the radix-4 datapath unmistakable from ISO
Add an FPGA die/package outline plus a heatsink so the silhouette reads instantly as an FPGA accelerator, not a generic PCB
Differentiate a forward-NTT vs inverse-NTT (INTT) annotation/path and vary primitives further (e.g. capsule pipeline FIFOs) for the geometry axis

meta.before: Build on an FPGA PCB substrate. Along the left edge place eight interleaved BRAM banks that hold polynomial coefficients under the conflict-free memory mapping scheme. A wide conflict-free crossbar network spans the banks and routes operands to four parallel radix-4 butterfly clusters, each housing a DSP modular multiplier and a modular add/sub ALU. Butterfly outputs pass through a shared modular-reduction unit back to the crossbar. On the right sit the twiddle-factor ROM, the address-generation unit implementing the mapping scheme, a radix-2/4 configuration selector, and a clock PLL. Input and output FIFOs flank the memory banks.
meta.after: 1) Start from the FPGA PCB substrate (14x9 m floorplan). 2) Along the left edge mount the eight interleaved BRAM banks at 1.1 m pitch and flank them with the input and output FIFOs. 3) Drop the conflict-free crossbar network as a vertical spine just inboard of the banks. 4) For each of the four parallel butterfly clusters, lay a baseplate, then populate it with a DSP modular multiplier, a symmetric modular adder, a symmetric modular subtractor, and a pipeline register. 5) Place the shared modular-reduction unit as a vertical spine to the right of the clusters, wired from every pipeline register back to the crossbar. 6) On the right, install the twiddle-factor ROM (feeding all multipliers), the address-generation unit, the radix-2/4 config selector, the schedule/FSM controller, and the clock PLL.
